name: Hohhot
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Hohhot: dairy and agrifood supply chains, polysilicon and data centre partners, integrity research.
hero_lede: Hohhot is the capital of Inner Mongolia and the base of two of the world's largest dairy companies, as well as a growing centre for polysilicon, data centres and veterinary pharmaceuticals. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, within the limits of Chinese law.
intro: Hohhot is the capital and administrative centre of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, with a permanent population of about 3.64 million and urbanisation above 80 percent, according to local government reporting in late 2025. Its administrative area covers four urban districts, four counties and one banner. City GDP was about 380 billion yuan in 2023, and services make up the largest share. Hohhot calls itself China's dairy capital: it is home to Yili and Mengniu, both among the world's ten largest dairy companies, and its dairy industry chain reported revenue of more than 256 billion yuan in 2024. The city also claims about 60 percent of national polysilicon capacity, a large data centre cluster and major veterinary vaccine and feed-additive plants.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Hohhot mainly through supply chains and investment. International food, ingredient and packaging companies supply or buy from the dairy groups and their many farms, feed suppliers and processors. Solar manufacturers and buyers of polysilicon need to understand ownership, energy sourcing and the compliance status of producers in the region, given US and other import restrictions on solar supply chains. Data centre and cloud projects draw contractors and investors. Integrity risk is part of the picture: a former Communist Party official of the Hohhot Economic and Technological Development Zone was sentenced to death in 2022 for embezzlement and bribery exceeding 3 billion yuan, a reminder of how development zones and land deals can concentrate corruption risk.

matters.title: Dairy supply chain diligence
matters.text: Hohhot's dairy cluster links the two national champions to farms, feed and forage suppliers, packaging firms and ingredient processors. We research the ownership, regulatory record, food safety history and litigation of suppliers and partners using public Chinese sources, so international buyers and sellers understand who they are dealing with.

matters.title: Polysilicon and solar compliance research
matters.text: With a large share of China's polysilicon capacity, Hohhot producers sit at the start of many solar supply chains. We map corporate ownership and affiliates, compare disclosed facility locations and inputs with public records, and screen against trade restriction lists to support counsel's import and supply chain compliance assessments.

matters.title: Data centre and cloud counterparties
matters.text: Hohhot promotes itself as a computing hub, attracting builders, operators and equipment suppliers. Before investment or contracting we review counterparties' registered capital, shareholders, administrative penalties, litigation and media coverage, and flag where Chinese data and cybersecurity rules may limit what a foreign party can see or do.

matters.title: Development zone and land integrity risk
matters.text: The Li Jianping case, involving more than 3 billion yuan of embezzlement and bribery linked to the Hohhot development zone, shows how land allocation and zone management can concentrate risk. We research counterparties' links to officials, enforcement actions and reported disciplinary cases using public sources.

matters.title: Veterinary pharmaceutical and feed additive partners
matters.text: Hohhot hosts large producers of animal vaccines, feed additives and fermentation ingredients that export worldwide. We review ownership, regulatory and product quality history, trade enforcement and disputes for distributors and buyers, scoped to what public Chinese and international records can lawfully show.

local_context.title: Courts in Hohhot
local_context.text: Hohhot is the seat of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region Higher People's Court, which hears appeals from intermediate courts across the region, and of the Hohhot Intermediate People's Court, which hears larger civil and commercial cases and appeals from the city's basic courts. Judgments are partly published online, though publication has narrowed in recent years. Chinese counsel advises on forum and procedure; we research parties and their litigation history from available records.

local_context.title: Arbitration and dispute resolution
local_context.text: Commercial contracts with Hohhot companies often provide for arbitration, either at a local arbitration commission in the city or at national or international institutions such as those in Beijing or Hong Kong. Counsel confirms the seat and rules named in the contract. We support counsel with research on counterparties' assets, affiliates and prior disputes, using lawful public and commercial sources.

local_context.title: Regional regulators and records
local_context.text: Company registration in Hohhot is handled by the local market regulation administration under the State Administration for Market Regulation, and core registration data, shareholders of record and administrative penalties appear in the national enterprise credit information system. Food safety, veterinary drug and environmental regulators at regional and city level publish inspections and penalties that are often central to diligence on dairy, pharmaceutical and industrial companies.

local_context.title: Data rules and on-the-ground limits
local_context.text: Chinese data protection, data security and counter-espionage laws apply in Hohhot as everywhere in mainland China, and there is no licensing regime for private investigators. Information-gathering on Chinese companies and individuals must be scoped carefully, transfers of personal information abroad are restricted, and some inquiries are inadvisable. We plan engagements with Chinese counsel and keep to public, lawfully obtained information.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office or staff in Hohhot or elsewhere in mainland China, and works on Hohhot matters from Nashville. We first agree with the client and its counsel the decision at stake, such as a dairy supply relationship, a polysilicon purchase, a data centre investment or a dispute, and assess the legal limits on gathering and transferring information about Chinese companies and individuals. Research relies on public registration data, regulatory penalty and court records, stock exchange disclosures by listed groups such as Yili and Mengniu, trade restriction lists, and Chinese and international media. We do not conduct covert inquiries in China, do not obtain non-public records and coordinate with Chinese counsel on any step taken in the country.

faqs.q: Why is Hohhot important for food and ingredient supply chains?
faqs.a: Hohhot is home to Yili and Mengniu, both among the world's ten largest dairy companies, and local reporting puts the city's dairy chain revenue above 256 billion yuan in 2024. Their suppliers, processors and partners extend across Inner Mongolia, so international companies in dairy, ingredients and packaging often need to review counterparties connected to the city.

faqs.q: Can you research polysilicon producers in Hohhot?
faqs.a: We can research ownership, affiliates, disclosed facilities, regulatory penalties, litigation and media coverage of producers, and screen them against trade restriction lists. This supports counsel assessing import and supply chain obligations. We work from public and commercial sources and do not visit facilities covertly or obtain non-public records in China.

faqs.q: What does the Li Jianping case show about local risk?
faqs.a: Li Jianping, a former Party official of the Hohhot Economic and Technological Development Zone, was sentenced to death in 2022 for embezzlement and bribery exceeding 3 billion yuan and executed in December 2024. The case shows how zone management and land allocation can concentrate corruption risk, so counterparties' links to officials and enforcement cases deserve attention.

faqs.q: Can a private investigator work in Hohhot?
faqs.a: Mainland China does not license private investigators, and information-gathering is constrained by data protection, data security and counter-espionage law. TDSC has no presence in China and does not carry out covert work there. We scope research to public, lawfully available information and coordinate with Chinese counsel on any step that needs to be taken in the country.

faqs.q: Which courts hear disputes involving Hohhot companies?
faqs.a: Larger civil and commercial cases are generally heard by the Hohhot Intermediate People's Court, with appeals to the Inner Mongolia Higher People's Court, also in Hohhot. Many contracts instead provide for arbitration in Hohhot, Beijing, Hong Kong or elsewhere. Counsel determines the forum; we research parties and their prior disputes.
